extracted.intended_audience: literary readers, critics, and poets; students of literature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what qualities make a great Poet and a great Poem, illustrated by readings of Dante and Shakespeare (musical thought, sincerity, intensity, vision, moral seriousness, form/content fit, structural harmony, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as musical Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: "Poetry, therefore, we will call musical Thought. The Poet is he who thinks in that manner."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry must be inwardly musical: the thought itself is sung. The work's worth depends on an underlying melody of meaning (Coleridge: a sentence musically worded signals depth). Example: Dante's Divina Commedia proceeds "as by a chant."

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and depth of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is a man's sincerity and depth of vision that makes him a Poet."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine, deeply-felt conviction is the primary measure of poetic worth. Works that come from the inmost heart endure; those of outer fashion do not. Example: Dante's sincerity renders his poem authentic and long-lasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of song — avoid false rhyme or jingle
rubrics_metrics.description: If one can speak the thought plainly, one should not sing it; rhyme without inward necessity is a "mere wooden noise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: using rhyme or sonorous form as ornament when the thought has no melodic need. Advice: only adopt sung/metrical forms when the heart's passion requires them; otherwise prefer plain speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity / concentrated genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Dante's prevailing characteristic is "intensity" — world-great because world-deep rather than world-wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A poet's power often lies in concentrated depth and fierce emphasis rather than encyclopaedic breadth. Measure: degree to which the work penetrates to the "heart of Being" and sustains concentrated force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of vision / pictorial vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet should have a "great power of vision; seizes the very type of a thing; presents that and nothing more."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for quick, decisive, emblematic images (e.g., the 'red-hot cone of iron' of Dite, 'fiery snow'). The ability to present the essence of a scene in vivid, condensed strokes is a mark of greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: "One smiting word; and then there is silence, nothing more said. His silence is more eloquent than words."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy of expression — extreme condensation and decisive phrasing — is prized. Excess verbiage dilutes power; the poet should cut to the essential likeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural harmony / structural symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: A true inward symmetry, an "architectural harmony," should govern the work; parts should proportionate and fit together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the poem's internal architecture (e.g., Inferno/Purgatorio/Paradiso as compartments that answer to one another). Cohesion, proportionality, and balance across sections indicate artistic completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral seriousness and rigor combined with pity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Infinite pity, yet also infinite rigor of law... a man who does not know rigor cannot pity either."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral depth: greatness blends tender pity with uncompromising moral rigor. Anti-pattern: sentimental pity lacking moral ballast (sentimentality). Examples: Dante's pity for sinners coupled with stern justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of belief / conviction in represented world
rubrics_metrics.description: Dante's supernatural world (Hell, Purgatory, Paradise) is treated as a real fact to him; that conviction makes the representation powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poet truly 'believes' the world they depict; authentic conviction gives symbolic or emblematic material life and prevents mere allegory from feeling contrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form suited to content (form–content unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The terza rima and the canto-like progression aided Dante's musical chant: form supports the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether metrical and formal choices arise from and reinforce the poem's inner temperament (e.g., chant-like stanza form for religious epic). Form should be necessary and organic, not imposed ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance / timelessness over immediate effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The worth of a work is not its worldly effect but that it issues from the inmost parts of a man's soul and so may 'last yet for long thousands of years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate greatness solely by contemporary influence or utilitarian outcomes. Prefer works speaking to perennial human depths; endurance across generations signals worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy with objects / sincerity in depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: To paint a true likeness the poet must have 'sympathized with it' — sincerity and sympathy enable authentic depiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs the poet has empathetic understanding of subjects (people, scenes, passions), rather than mere superficial reporting or hearsay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and meticulous elaboration of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Every compartment of Dante's work is 'worked out, with intense earnestness, into truth, into clear visuality... Each answers to the other; each fits in its place.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether each section is developed with care and whether details cohere into the larger design. Meticulous workmanship and internal fit are marks of a completed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of social representation (Shakspeare's competence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspeare 'embodies for us the Outer Life of our Europe' — chivalries, courtesies, humors, ambitions; he records the practical way of thinking and acting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A different criterion: scope and fidelity in portraying the social/psychological life of an age. Measure how comprehensively the poet or dramatist renders the outward manners and practices of a society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor and suffering as source of true thought
rubrics_metrics.description: "Thought, true labor of any kind, highest virtue itself, is it not the daughter of Pain?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine poetic insight typically arises from sustained effort and suffering; works produced by deep struggle often have greater depth than those produced easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emblematic representation grounded in lived conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Dante's Hell/Purgatory/Paradise function as emblematic representations of Christian moral law because they originate in sincere belief rather than contrived allegory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between mere allegory and emblematic representation that feels organically rooted in the poet's worldview. The latter has moral and imaginative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of utility as sole standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is not by what is called their effect on the world... that a man and his work are measured."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reduce artistic value to social or political impact. A poem's measure may be its inward truth and beauty rather than its immediate usefulness or influence.
